lr.name: Land records
lr.notice: Land records keeps what the register says beside what is drawn and what was walked. A phone or a watch places a point within a few meters at best: a walk is a sketch of a boundary, not a survey. Only a licensed surveyor and the land registry fix a boundary. The papers it fills are outlines for you to check, not any authority's form.

lr.walk.help: Walk the land with a phone and press one button at each corner. Open this drawing on the phone, switch this add-on on there, and press Start a walk. A watch, a headset button or a Bluetooth clicker can press the button for you. A route recorded by a watch or another app comes in as a GPX file.

lr.w.remote.on: Ready. The watch shows "Field walk" as what is playing: play, pause or next marks a corner, previous removes the last one. A clicker's Page Down or Enter marks too. The sound is silence.

lr.w.notice: Stand still on each corner for {s} seconds, then press. A press is refused when the device says it is off by more than {max} m. This is a sketch of the land, not a survey: a phone is rarely closer than a few meters, worse under trees and beside buildings.

lr.w.err.timeout: The device is taking long to find its position. Keep waiting outdoors.
lr.w.err.insecure: A browser gives the position only to a page opened over https.

lr.check.help: Compares each parcel as drawn with the area its record states, and looks for parcels that share ground, corners that nearly meet a neighbor's line, outlines that cross themselves and numbers used twice. It compares; it does not say which figure is right. The tolerances are yours.

lr.rule.title: Your lot rules
lr.rule.help: Limits you have read in the rules that apply, typed by you: the smallest lot and the shortest street frontage, for one land use or for every lot. New lots are checked against them. Frontage is measured on the street line named in a parcel's zoning; without one it is not checked.
lr.rule.err: Type a smallest lot area or a shortest frontage.
lr.rule.pass: Every new lot meets your lot rules.
lr.doc.help: Fills a paper from a proposal: its parcels before and after, the areas, the reason, and the details you type once. A value nobody stated prints as "[not stated: …]" and is listed here; nothing is made up.
lr.doc.err.pack: That file is not a template pack this add-on can read.
lr.doc.pick: Keep a proposal under Change parcels first, then choose it in the list there.
lr.doc.complete: Every field the paper asks for is stated. Read it through before you send it.
lr.doc.html: Save as a page to print
lr.doc.print: Open the saved page in a browser and print it, or save it as PDF from the print window.

lr.rulemsg.minfrontage: {lot} has {value} m of frontage, under your shortest of {limit} m.

lr.site.help: What stands on each parcel and what there is to measure. The buildings are the building masses of this drawing (Massing): their footprints are laid over the parcels, so each lot shows its footprint, floor area, coverage and floor area ratio. Only the part of a footprint that is on a lot counts for that lot, and its floor area is taken in the same share. The quantities file opens in TakeoffCraft.
lr.site.totals: {lots} lots, {area}. Boundary on the ground: {boundary} (a line two lots share is counted once; {shared} is shared). Distinct corners: {corners}.
lr.site.straddles: Only {pct} % of the footprint is on this parcel
lr.site.none: No building masses in this drawing. Draw them in Massing and they are counted here.

lr.place.help: The lot minimums, legal figures and forms of one place, as data with the document, the clause and how each figure was read. A place comes as its own add-on (Settings › Add-ons) or as a rules file you open. The lots are compared with what the text prints; it is not a ruling. Width is measured on the street line named in the lot's zoning, depth from that line: the place's own definition of width and depth governs.
lr.place.nopacks: No place's rules are switched on. Add a rules add-on for your place in Settings › Add-ons, or open a rules file.
lr.place.missing: This drawing was set to the rules "{id}", which are not switched on here. Nothing is compared until they are.
lr.place.err.file: That file is not a rules file this add-on can read.

lr.ifc.title: Buildings from an IFC model
lr.ifc.help: Read the buildings of an IFC file from any BIM program. Each building's elements are laid flat on the plan and its outline is traced, true to about the grid size shown (5 cm unless the model is very large). Ground a building encloses counts as footprint. Floor area is the model's own figure where it states one, else its floor slabs added up, else footprint times storeys. A file with a map position lands where it belongs; any other is placed by the three numbers below.

lr.mk.title: Mark up in MarkupCraft
lr.mk.help: Makes the parcel plan as a PDF at a round scale and the open notes as a BCF file placed on that sheet. Open the PDF in MarkupCraft, then import the BCF file there: each note lands on its spot. When the sheet comes back, export BCF from MarkupCraft and read it here: a note still at its place takes its new status and comments, and a note added on the sheet becomes a note on the plan.
lr.mk.save: Save the plan and the notes
lr.mk.sub: {date}. {lots} lots, {notes} notes. A plan for marking up, not a survey.
lr.mk.empty: Nothing to put on a sheet yet: the drawing has no parcels.
